answer: Bound the query along four dimensions. (1) Shape and cycle state: allow only declared edge types and direction, and decide whether paths are node-simple or relationship-simple. Carry visited state so a reached node or edge is not expanded again - for example a recursive CTE with a depth counter below N plus a visited-array guard such as `NOT (e.dst = ANY(w.visited))`. Cypher's default path uniqueness is relationship-based, so it does not by itself enforce node-simple paths. (2) Resource caps: set a maximum hop count, maximum result cardinality and a per-request resource budget (time, memory, visited state); check depth before expansion and stop at the cap. A high-degree hub can make a path search expensive even when the graph has few total nodes. (3) Answer contract: state whether the output is all paths, any path, shortest path or only reachable node IDs; when the question is existential reachability, stop at the first hit and return DISTINCT endpoint IDs instead of enumerating paths. (4) Exhaustion behavior: return a partial result with an explicit truncation flag or an error, and never report "no path" when the budget was exhausted. Apply time-validity and authorization checks to intermediate nodes and edges, not only the endpoint; repeated traversal around a cycle is not extra evidence.
